interactions.note: The epitope-specific nanobody Nb-ER14 bound to BabA-expressing H. pylori cells, demonstrating that the conformation of Nb-stabilized BabA(AD) is equivalent to that of native BabA in the bacterial outer membrane.
The epitope-specific nanobody Nb-ER14 bound to BabA adhesion domain (AD) and stabilized the protein, as shown by an increase in the melting temperature of BabA(AD) in the presence of nanobody.

The epitope of nanobody Nb-ER14 on BabA adhesion domain (AD) was determined from the crystal structure of the complex. There are two BabA(AD) and two Nb-ER14 copies per asymmetric unit. Crystal growth was facilitated with the nanobody generated against native BabA purified from H. pylori found to stabilize the recombinant BabA(AD) fragment.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 2.74 angstroms

The epitope of nanobody Nb-ER19 on BabA adhesion domain (AD) of Helicobacter pylori strain A730 in complex with blood group H Lewis b hexasaccharide was determined from the crystal structure of the complex. In this hybrid construct of BabA (AD), the insertion domain (residues 179-258) of the Alaskan strain A730, responsible for carbohydrate binding, was grafted into the framework of the generalist strain 17875. Crystal growth was facilitated with the nanobody generated against native BabA purified from H. pylori found to stabilize the recombinant BabA(AD) fragment.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 2.99 angstroms
